mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has shifted from negative to positive (t-0w: +2.6%), signaling restored consumer confidence in essential shopping. This confidence spillover drives discretionary RETAIL_REC visits upward over the next four weeks as consumers resume normal shopping patterns.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM crossed from negative to positive at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts to negative values within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined monotonically from +10.7% to +8.3% over four weeks, indicating accelerating exit from home confinement. This sustained outflow from residential spaces directly drives increased RETAIL_REC mobility as people resume out-of-home activities.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or plateaus in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has improved from -23.0% to -19.1% over four weeks. When TRANSIT recovers above -20%, commuting infrastructure capacity enables retail district accessibility, which directly amplifies RETAIL_REC visits in the subsequent four-week period.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved to -19.1% at t-0w, crossing -20% threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility falls below -20% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite TRANSIT remaining above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -8.7% to -4.3% over four weeks, indicating return to office routines. Concurrent improvement in TRANSIT (-23.0% to -19.1%) enables commuter access to retail districts. The interaction of workplace return and transit recovery jointly drives RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent improvement over four weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses to prior-week levels, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite both proxies improving.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained severely depressed (-20.6% at t-0w) despite modest recovery in other categories, indicating continued outdoor-activity restrictions. evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -20.6% at t-0w, showing no recovery trend
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -15% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite PARKS remaining restricted.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved from -18.1% to -14.1% over four weeks, showing consistent week-on-week recovery momentum. This trend acceleration, independent of external drivers, indicates autonomous demand recovery that will sustain RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.0 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses to -16% or lower in the next two weeks, or the four-week forward mean does not exceed the four-week backward mean.
